title: Lancashire Butter Pie
subtitle: A simple shortcrust pie of potato and onion, rich with butter
excerpt: Sliced potato and soft onion layered inside a shortcrust case with plenty of butter. An old Lancashire staple that is more than the sum of its parts.
sourceNotes: Traditional Lancashire vegetarian pie from the Preston and Chorley area, historically served on meatless Fridays.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until piping hot throughout.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie the day before and bake when needed. It also keeps well cold for packed lunches.

content.text: Lancashire butter pie is a local classic with nothing but potato, onion and butter inside. The key is cooking the onion until properly soft before layering. Underdone onion makes the filling watery and sharp.

items.prepNote: two thirds base, one third lid

content.text: Melt 40g of the butter in a frying pan over a low heat. Cook the onions for 15 minutes, stirring often, until completely soft and pale gold. Season and set aside to cool.
Parboil the potato slices in salted water for 4 minutes until just starting to bend. Drain and cool on a clean tea towel.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish. Leave a little overhang.
Layer half the potato into the pie case. Spread the onions over. Add the rest of the potato. Dot with the remaining 20g of butter and season well.
Roll the remaining pastry for the lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg. Lay the lid on top and press the edges firmly together. Trim and crimp.
Brush the top with beaten egg. Cut two slits in the centre to let steam escape. Bake for 50 minutes until deep gold.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes before slicing. This allows the filling to settle and the pastry to firm up.

items.cause: The potato was not dried after parboiling, or the onion was not cooked long enough.
items.fix: Always drain and dry the potato. Cook the onion until all liquid has evaporated before layering.

items.cause: The oven rack was too high, or the filling was too wet.
items.fix: Place the pie on a baking tray and cook on the lower third of the oven for a crisper base.

items.symptom: The potato is hard inside after baking.
items.cause: The slices were too thick or the parboil too short.
items.fix: Slice potato thinly (about 3mm) and parboil for a full 4 minutes before assembling.
